title: Clean drinking water in every public school
tagline: Thirty schools still run on pipes laid before 1970.
short_description: A district-by-district push to replace lead service lines in the thirty oldest public schools in the county.
long_description:
Thirty schools in this county still draw drinking water through service lines installed before 1970. Testing last spring found elevated lead in eleven of them.

The replacement programme is already funded at the state level, but districts have to apply, and most do not have the grant staff to do it. This campaign pays for the outreach that gets those applications filed before the deadline.
why_backers_should_care: The money to fix this already exists. What is missing is anyone telling the districts it is there.
target_audience: Parents and school-board voters in the county, aged 28 to 55.
ad_headline: Eleven schools. Elevated lead. One deadline.
ad_primary_text: The state will pay to replace the pipes, but only if the district applies. Most have not. Here is why.

title: Redraw the bus network around where people actually work
tagline: The map has not changed since the factories closed.
short_description: Most routes still converge downtown, but the jobs moved to the ring road a decade ago. This is the case for redrawing them.
long_description:
The current network was designed for a downtown that employed forty thousand people. It now employs eleven thousand. Meanwhile the warehouse and hospital corridor on the ring road employs twenty-six thousand, and is served by two buses an hour.

The transit authority has a redesign sitting in a drawer. It needs public comment to move.
why_backers_should_care: A redesign costs nothing to adopt. It is the same buses, the same drivers, a different map.
target_audience: Transit riders and ring-road commuters in the metro area.
ad_headline: The buses still go where the jobs used to be.
ad_primary_text: Twenty-six thousand jobs. Two buses an hour. The redesign is written, it just needs you.

title: Let farmers repair the equipment they own
tagline: A $400 sensor can idle a $400,000 combine for three weeks.
short_description: Software locks mean a dealer technician has to authorise repairs farmers used to do themselves. A state bill would change that.
long_description:
Modern agricultural equipment refuses to run after some repairs until a dealer technician connects and authorises the part. During harvest, the wait for that technician averages eleven days.

Four states have passed right-to-repair laws covering farm equipment. A fifth bill is in committee here.
why_backers_should_care: This is not anti-manufacturer. It is about who holds the key to equipment someone already bought.
target_audience: Rural voters and independent farm operators statewide.
ad_headline: You own the combine. You do not own the password.
ad_primary_text: An eleven-day wait for a dealer technician, mid-harvest. Four states already fixed this.

title: Keep the winter shelter open past 7am
tagline: Everyone is turned out at dawn, including in a freeze warning.
short_description: The shelter closes at 7am year-round under a rule written in 1998. Extending hours during freeze warnings costs less than one night of emergency calls.
long_description:
Under the current operating agreement the shelter empties at 7am regardless of conditions. On freeze-warning mornings, emergency services log an average of nine cold-exposure calls between 7am and noon.

Keeping the doors open on those mornings costs roughly $340. A single ambulance transport costs more.
why_backers_should_care: The cheaper option and the humane option are the same option here, which is rarer than it should be.
ad_headline: Turned out at 7am into a freeze warning.
ad_primary_text: Nine cold-exposure calls a morning. Staying open costs $340. A transport costs more.

title: Write ballot measures at a tenth-grade reading level
tagline: The last measure needed a graduate degree to parse.
short_description: Five of seven measures on the last ballot scored above college reading level. Plain-language summaries are cheap, legal and already used elsewhere.
long_description:
An independent readability analysis of the last county ballot put five of seven measures above a college reading level, and two above graduate level.

Nine states require a plain-language summary alongside the legal text. Adopting the same standard here needs a single administrative rule change.
why_backers_should_care: A ballot nobody can read is a turnout problem disguised as a drafting problem.
target_audience: Registered voters across the county, all ages.
ad_headline: Could you read the last ballot? Honestly?
ad_primary_text: Five of seven measures scored above college reading level. Nine states already fixed this.

title: Plant the shade where the heat actually is
tagline: The hottest blocks have the fewest trees. That is not a coincidence.
short_description: Surface temperatures vary by up to 11C across the city. The canopy budget is currently split evenly by district rather than by need.
long_description:
Thermal mapping last August found an 11C spread in surface temperature between the shadiest and least-shaded blocks. The least-shaded are concentrated in four neighbourhoods.

The canopy budget is allocated evenly across nine districts, which means the hottest blocks receive the same funding as the coolest.
why_backers_should_care: Even distribution and fair distribution are not the same thing when the starting points differ this much.
target_audience: City residents in the four highest-heat neighbourhoods, plus climate-engaged voters.
ad_primary_text: The canopy budget is split evenly by district. The heat is not spread evenly at all.
